cards.name: Zoom - 3D tumble
cards.summary: Transition-in: the layer starts at 0% scale and tumbles in 3D (Basic 3D swivel 360 deg on Y, tilt 60 deg on X) while zooming up to fill the frame, landing flat and square at 100%.
use_for: Pop a photo, screenshot or news card into frame over a background plate
Playful sticker / logo entrance in social reels
Retro TV-news DVE style move for satire segments
avoid: Looks dated and cheesy on documentary or serious political footage
Needs a layer underneath to read as a transition; on its own it reveals over black/transparent
Fast Y spin smears faces and on-screen text mid-move
cards.duration_note: Pseudo-effect 'Zoom - 3D tumble' > 'Transition Completion' keys 0 at comp.time -> 100 at about +1.0 s (2 keys). Scale (Transform effect) and the motion are expressions driven by that slider, so before comp.time the layer is at scale 0 (invisible) and after +1 s it holds at 100%. Times decoded from the .ffx keyframe data (23976 ticks/s), so treat them as +/-1 frame.
cards.scripting: Set comp.time to the transition start (layer.inPoint for an IN), deselect all layers, set layer.selected = true, then layer.applyPreset(new File(<preset .ffx path>)) (applyPreset acts on every selected layer, so isolate the target first); keyframe times are relative to comp.time. Stack this incoming layer ABOVE the outgoing clip with an overlap at least as long as the transition: it reveals itself over whatever is below (transparent/black if nothing). Effect and control names this preset creates start with a TAB character (e.g. '\tTransition Completion'), and the rig's expressions reference those exact names: do not rename them, and strip the leading tab when searching by name. The master control is ADBE CM Zoom3DTumble (registered in Support Files/PresetEffects.xml, hidden from the Effects menu); find it by that match name. Adding it by match name gives the bare control only - the preset is what wires the expressions. Controls: 'Transition Completion' (ADBE CM Zoom3DTumble-0001, keyed 0 -> 100 = layer arrives), 'X tumble' (-0002, 60 deg, drives Basic 3D Tilt) and 'Y tumble' (-0003, 360 deg, drives Basic 3D Swivel); both unwind linearly to 0. Set both to 0 for a plain zoom-in. The Transform effect's Anchor Point/Position follow the layer anchor point. Retime by moving key 2 of -0001. To use it as an OUT transition, apply at (outPoint - duration) and swap the two keyframe values of the driver property (prop.setValueAtKey(1, v2); prop.setValueAtKey(2, v1)).

verified.note: At 0.5 s the shot is small, tilted and mirrored mid-swivel over black, and by 1.4 s it sits flat at full size.

cards.name: Band Wipe - Build HD
cards.summary: Mask-based reveal: seven horizontal bands (each ~1/7 of the 1080 px height) wipe in one after another, each growing from the LEFT edge to full width, top band first, so the image builds top to bottom over ~2 s.
use_for: Build a full-frame graphic or map in stages in an explainer
Stepped reveal of a headline plate in a news package
Rhythmic reveal cut on beats in a trailer
avoid: HD-only: wrong coverage on 1080x1920 reels or 4K layers
The layer is invisible before the first keyframe: apply at the layer's in point, not mid-clip
Hard-edged bands look like old broadcast DVE
cards.duration_note: 7 masks, each animating for about 0.29 s (7 frames at 24 fps), staggered back-to-back: band 1 starts at comp.time and the last band finishes at about +2.04 s. Before its keys each band mask has zero width, so the layer is invisible before comp.time. Times decoded from the .ffx keyframe data (23976 ticks/s), so treat them as +/-1 frame.
cards.scripting: Set comp.time to the transition start (layer.inPoint for an IN), deselect all layers, set layer.selected = true, then layer.applyPreset(new File(<preset .ffx path>)) (applyPreset acts on every selected layer, so isolate the target first); keyframe times are relative to comp.time. Stack this incoming layer ABOVE the outgoing clip with an overlap at least as long as the transition: it reveals itself over whatever is below (transparent/black if nothing). Adds 7 masks (Mask 1-7, mode Add, hard edges) whose vertices are fixed 1920x1080 coordinates (decoded as +/-960 x +/-540 around the layer centre): on a vertical 1080x1920 reel or a 4K clip they do not cover the whole layer - precompose the layer into a 1920x1080 comp first. Existing Add masks on the layer combine with them. Retime by moving the keys of layer.property('ADBE Mask Parade').property(i).property('ADBE Mask Shape') (i = 1..7). No effects are added. To use as an OUT, apply at (outPoint - duration) and time-reverse the mask-shape keys.
cards.equivalent: Premiere: Band Wipe transition (closest; Premiere's bands slide in together from alternating sides)

verified.note: Horizontal bands of about 1/7 frame height fill one at a time from the left edge, top first: band 2 is part-way across at 0.5 s and band 5 is part-way at 1.4 s, with black below.

cards.name: Barn Doors
cards.summary: Reveal: the incoming layer appears from the left and right edges as two hard-edged 'doors' that close toward the vertical centre line until the shot below is covered. Two Linear Wipes (90 / -90 deg, each driven 0 -> 51%) followed by Invert (Alpha), so the wiped-away areas are what shows; driven by a 'Wipe Master Control 1' slider.
use_for: Symmetrical scene change between two B-roll shots
Close in on a title card or chapter plate in an explainer
Dramatic 'doors shut' beat in a trailer
avoid: Invert (Alpha) flips existing transparency: on a cut-out PNG, logo or text layer the transparent areas turn opaque - use on full-frame footage only
The layer is invisible before the first keyframe: apply at the layer's in point, not mid-clip
Hard edges (Feather 0) look dated; raise Feather on both Linear Wipes for a softer look
cards.duration_note: 'Wipe Master Control' > 'Transition Completion' keys 0 at comp.time -> 100 at about +1.0 s; each Linear Wipe completion = linear(0..100 -> 0..51). Layer invisible before comp.time. Times decoded from the .ffx keyframe data (23976 ticks/s), so treat them as +/-1 frame.

Effect and control names this preset creates start with a TAB character (e.g. '\tTransition Completion'), and the rig's expressions reference those exact names: do not rename them, and strip the leading tab when searching by name. The master control is ADBE CM TransWipe (registered in Support Files/PresetEffects.xml, hidden from the Effects menu); find it by that match name. Adding it by match name gives the bare control only - the preset is what wires the expressions. Here the control is named 'Wipe Master Control 1' (with ' 1'): 'Transition Completion' (ADBE CM TransWipe-0001, keyed 0 -> 100 = fully covered). Effect order matters: the Invert must stay after both Linear Wipes. Direction (edges closing inward) read from the wipe angles and the alpha Invert, not rendered. To use it as an OUT transition, apply at (outPoint - duration) and swap the two keyframe values of the driver property (prop.setValueAtKey(1, v2); prop.setValueAtKey(2, v1)).

verified.note: At 0.5 s the shot shows as two hard-edged strips at the left and right edges with a black gap in the middle closing in, and it fills the frame by 1.4 s.

Right Bottom), turning Clockwise / Counterclockwise / Both ('Direction' dropdown), erases the layer to reveal what is below.
